context: Request: the firm's deals over $1B in guaranteed (base) consideration, excluding earnout/CVR value, governed by Delaware law. Rubric: 1001-00004, 1003-00003, 1038-00009, 1041-00003 as qualifying, plus a precision criterion. 1038-00001 (a litigation matter whose case assessment describes a ~$4.7B Delaware-law merger) and 1025-00006 / 1018-00003 ($925M plus CVR) are outside the set.

runs.failure_point: It added a litigation matter to the qualifying set on a case-assessment snippet, after the scan review had named that weak evidence.

first_error.why: It counted a litigation matter as a qualifying deal from a case-assessment snippet giving a deal value and the requested clause (evidence seen at [56]-[57]), without opening any executed agreement for it.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [74] said that matter was confirmed only from a case assessment, not the operative agreement's governing-law clause; the agent wrote it anyway, and the later check reviews told it not to add or drop matters.

divergence: Mixed (T0, T2 pass; T1 fails on precision). All three runs reached the four qualifying deals and read their executed agreements. They split at the verification stage after the store-wide scan: T0 and T2 judged candidates only from executed agreement text, while T1 ran its snippet script over a hand-picked list that included a litigation matter and accepted that matter's deal value and clause from a case assessment. The critic's review there differed from the passing runs: it named this exact weakness, but the agent wrote the matter as qualifying, and the later check reviews (which said not to add or drop matters) did not press the point again.
